TROOP.

label: text
text: UR M. GOLLAN'S INTEREST.

label: text
text: Challenge Cup Prevented for Annual Competition.

label: text
text:
The No. 6 Hongkong (Elms Kadoorie School) Troop of Boy Scouts gathered at the School hall at Sookumpoo yesterday afternoon to welcome Sir Henry Gollan, the Chief Justice, who has shewn a keen interest in the movement by presenting a challenge cup for inter-patrol competition annually.
In the awarding of the new to

label: text
text: In the awarding of the cup to the winning patrol, special attention will be paid to efficiency, attendance and conduct.

label: text
text: Sir Henry Gollan was met at the School gate by a guard of honour and proceeded to inspect the Troop. He then visited the Troop room and signed his name in the book.

label: text
text: The party, which consisted of the Hon. Mr. A. E. Wood (Director of Education), Mr. F. J. de Rome (Headmaster), the Rev. G. T. Waldegrave (Scout Commissioner), Scoutmaster T. K. S. Leung, Assistant Scoutmaster Yu, and masters of the School, adjourned with Sir Henry to the hull where the Scouts gave a display in signalling and ambulance work.

label: text
text:
Mr. de Rome, thanked Sir Henry Gollan for his attendance and interest in the Troop and spoke to the Scouts on the value of maintaining the efficiency of the Troop.
Sir Henry Gollan then addressed the gathering and presented the challenge cup. This was followed by a short speech by the Scoutmaster. The Scout Commissioner in a speech traced the history of the Troop, which was a good one, and commented on the Scout movement which was not only local but world-wide.

label: text
text: The various speeches were interpreted by Mr. K. S. Lam, who has just retired from the Scoutmastership of the Troop after several years' good service.

label: text
text: Cheers were then called for and the gathering dispersed after the singing of the British and Chinese national anthems.

label: text
text: This morning in the harbour there were indications of anticipations of the arrival of the typhoon which is slowly moving in the direction of Hongkong, although it is thought that it may curve northwards in the direction of Swatow before it arrives here.

label: text
text: The rescue tug was to be observed with steam up and ready for emergency this morning and the funnelless H.M.S. "Ambrose," undergoing its annual overhaul was moved to the buoy. for greater security.

label: text
text: If the typhoon does not diverge from its present path it is expected here on Sunday.

label: text
text: The Chinese cruiser "Hai Yung" which was to have left for Pratas yesterday at 1 p.m. with Hongkong officials aboard is still in harbour, wireless messages having been exchanged between the vessel and Pratas as a result of which it was decided that it would be dangerous to attempt to make the shoal for the present. The typhoon had not, at the time of the message, reached Pratas but seas were very high and wind force 5 and increasing. Preliminary arrangements are that the party which is to witness the inauguration of the wireless station on the shoal will leave on Tuesday next.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: DRIVER INJURED:

label: text
text: Mr. W. Curtis, of the Duro Garage, had a remarkable escape from severe injury yesterday when travelling in a car which was being towed from Taipo after a breakdown. A Chinese driver who was with him was seriously hurt and was conveyed to the Kwong Wah Hospital.

label: text
text: The accident was due to the tow rope breaking, the impetus carrying the car over the edge of the road down the steep incline on to the foreshore (at the straight stretch of road running parallel to the sea front at Shatin). The car descended with force on to the rocks below and Mr. Curtis and the driver were thrown out despite the fact that the hood was up.

label: text
text: A breakdown gang which went out later in the day to salvage the car found it impracticable in view of difficulty of access, the income tide and the damage sustained, to do other than retrieve certain undamaged parts.

label: text
text: Upon enquiry at the Kwong Wah this morning we were informed that the driver was progressing favourably.

label: paragraph_title
text: ENTERING ON THE LAST

label: text
text: PREMIER'S OPINIONS

label: text
text: The Prime Minister, in a letter wishing success to Mr. Sam Howard, the Conservative candidate in the by-election at Wallsend, refers at length to the coal stoppage. He recalls that the Government proposed to give effect to the whole of the recommendations of the Royal Commission's report, provided that the other parties also accepted the report and that this proposal was viewed with approval by the leaders of the Trade Unions Congress. Unhappily, the adherence of the miners' leaders to their policy of refusing to consider any concessions had prevented their accepting the Government's offer and the Government consequently had had to proceed along other lines.

label: text
text: But it was still engaged in making many of the recommendations of the Royal Commission's operative. The Prime Minister expressed the hope that some reduction of costs might be effected by the various reconstruction schemes which were recommended in the Royal Commission's report and were being assisted so far as the Government could do so by the Mining Industry Bill. But these re-organisation schemes could not have full effect for some time, and meanwhile the Royal Commission had definitely recommended some sacrifice on the part of the men.

label: text
text: The Prime Minister concludes: "When once I get any indication from those who have authority to speak on behalf of the men that they are prepared to consider such temporary sacrifice on the part of better paid men I can assure the electors of Wallsend that the Government will do all it can to obtain a full discussion of any reasonable proposals, and it is my sincere hope and belief that the crisis in the coal industry may be solved; before much more time has elapsed, on the basis of mutual interest and goodwill."

label: text
text: This last sentence of the Prime iMnister's letter is regarded as supporting the opinion which is generally held in the Parliamentary lobbies that the struggle is now entering upon the last phase.

label: paragraph_title
text: Church Intervention.

label: text
text: One difficulty in the way of these proposals is that the Government is unlikely to continue a subsidy for the period which would involve a charge of £10,000,000.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Meanwhile, however, members of the miners' Executive left London this afternoon for their districts. One of them, before his departure, expressed the belief that there would be new negotiations next week, but he thought that if these came about it would be through the intervention of the Bishops and the Free Church leaders. He declared that the Miners' Executive had accepted the proposals of the latter. The principal of these proposals are that work should be resumed on the conditions existing before the stoppage for another four months, whilst the negotiations going, the Government continuing the subsidy and the two sides agreeing to leave outstanding matters to arbitration.
